sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors are GOV5, MOAT5, REV8, DUR6, CAP5, CASH6, BAL NS, EXEC6 and EARN7; price-dependent R NS, D3, P NS and L NS. Every factor includes two material facts, contrary evidence, confidence and source/evidence IDs in the canonical audit. GQS means Growth Quality, not governance; P means price-implied expectations, not predictability.

Exact Decimal BQS known contribution is 5.24 with 92% coverage and mathematical missing-factor bounds 5.32–6.04; there is no BQS point. GQS is 0.40×8 + 0.20×6 + 0.15×7 + 0.15×5 + 0.10×6 = 6.80, displayed 6.8 with 100% factor coverage. IAS has only D's 0.20×3 = 0.60 known contribution, 20% coverage and broad missing-factor bounds 1.40–8.60. These are mathematical bounds, not confidence intervals or sortable midpoint scores. Reusing BQS's nested range would narrow IAS's algebraic bounds, but would still not create an IAS point.

No governance cap is applied: neither GOV≤3 nor a G1 failure is established. No funding-failure cap is imposed because G3 is unresolved rather than evidenced Fail. No GQS≤5 cash/capital override applies: CAP5 and CASH6 do not meet that trigger, and historical conversion is not persistently poor. Material G2 uncertainty excludes numerical quality/growth ranking even though the growth arithmetic is retained for transparency. Moving CAP and CASH independently by ±1 shifts GQS by ±0.15 and ±0.10, respectively; jointly its range is 6.55–7.05, which is economically more important than a decimal ranking difference. [E03–E16]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The company manufactures plastic moulded automotive parts and subassemblies for Tier-I suppliers, which in turn supply passenger-vehicle OEMs. Interior cabin trims, exterior plastics, under-hood components and HVAC ducts serve both ICE and electric vehicles. It manufactures to customer designs and specifications rather than owning the final vehicle platform or distribution channel. Operations began around FY2011; the current operating footprint is at Sanand, Gujarat, with a second unit planned at GIDC Sanand-II. Thirty injection-moulding machines span roughly 120–1,700 tonnes of clamping capacity; this machine rating is not the same measure as annual finished-product tonnage.

Economics arise from machine utilization, cycle time, yield, automation, labour productivity and local just-in-time service. Revenue is sale of manufactured goods net of GST; value added must be assessed after resin and production labour, not confused with gross invoice value. Customers approve material vendors and formulations; the prospectus says resin-price movements are generally reflected in customer pricing, reducing but not eliminating timing and working-capital risk. Nearly all FY26 revenue was generated in Gujarat, and the top five customers supplied 97.32% of sales. Receivables and inventory are funded partly by trade payables and borrowing. This is an operationally understandable business, but intelligibility does not by itself clear an integrity or solvency gate. [S5][S6]

sections.title: Moat and Industry Position
sections.text:
Qualification, consistent moulding quality, traceability and proximity to Tier-I assembly plants create useful switching friction. A replacement supplier must buy machines, develop tooling/process capability and pass customer trials; an exact cost or qualification period was not disclosed and is not invented. Existing utilization of 93.73% and rising tonnage show that the supplier is commercially relevant. Customer-directed resourcing, cost reduction or a change in vehicle program can erode that position. Customer specifications and approved vendors constrain bargaining power. Top-one concentration fell from 49.94% to 30.99% between FY24 and FY26, but top-five dependence barely changed. Certifications and a Tata vendor-park address do not establish proprietary technology or a structural cost advantage.

Machino Plastics is the closest primary comparator: FY26 revenue of ₹492.16 crore, operating EBITDA of ₹36.20 crore and PAT of ₹1.32 crore show that larger scale need not guarantee strong net profitability. Its annual report separates FY25 PAT of ₹8.5561 crore from comprehensive income of ₹8.8540 crore, which Kheria's prospectus peer table labels PAT. The distinction is preserved rather than using inflated peer earnings. PPAP Automotive is another automotive-plastics comparator, with prospectus FY26 revenue of ₹567.05 crore and operating EBITDA of ₹51.49 crore. Its PAT is not normalized here and its multiple is not transferred. Shaily is a capability benchmark for precision moulding and higher-value healthcare/device engineering, but its IP, exports and end-market mix make it unsuitable as a direct P/E anchor. These are economic comparisons, not an unqualified peer ranking.

ACMA's dated FY25 release reports 9.6% industry growth and 10% domestic OEM-component growth. Kheria outgrew this broad measure in FY25, but the product/geographic denominator needed to calculate accessible market share was not verified. No top-three or niche-leader label is asserted. [S6][S11][P1][P2]

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Scale
sections.text:
Reported revenue increased from ₹34.6685 crore in FY22 to ₹49.9402 crore in FY23, ₹62.3193 crore in FY24, ₹92.0717 crore in FY25 and ₹120.0147 crore in FY26. Annual additions were ₹15.2717, ₹12.3791, ₹29.7524 and ₹27.9430 crore. The selected three-year FY23–FY26 CAGR is 33.95%; the four-year context CAGR is 36.40%. Five- and ten-year CAGRs are ND because the required six/eleven comparable observations were not located. FY26 YoY growth was 30.35%, after 47.74% in FY25. No single-quarter annualization or invented TTM is used.

Production rose from 3,215 tonnes in FY24 to 4,154 in FY25 and 5,061.45 in FY26, a 25.47% two-year volume CAGR. Revenue per produced tonne rose from about ₹1.94 lakh to ₹2.37 lakh, reflecting price/mix rather than solely physical demand. FY24–FY26 reported revenue CAGR of 38.77% therefore exceeds volume growth. The disclosed gross-profit measure, after material consumption, inventory change and employee expense, increased from ₹16.2852 crore to ₹31.9414 crore. This corroborates rising value added, although it is not a conventional materials-only gross profit. No acquisitions were identified, but exact resin-price, new-product and customer-win contributions are not separately quantified. REV starts at 9 under the ≥30% schedule and is capped at 8 for the shorter, Medium-confidence record. There is no extra small-base discount or TAM-driven upgrade. [S1][S5–S7]

sections.title: Growth Quality and Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The accessible near-term runway is tangible but finite: existing capacity of 5,400 tonnes was 93.73% utilized in FY26, and the announced new unit adds 2,400 tonnes to reach 7,800. Construction, equipment installation, customer trials and regulatory approvals precede revenue. Management targets approvals/trials by December 2026 and commercial production in January 2027. These are forward milestones, not completed outcomes as of 20 October. Several post-construction licences and consent-to-operate were not yet obtained in the prospectus.

The central economic tension is full capital cost. The project budget is ₹65.1685 crore, including land, civil structure, machinery, utilities and contingency. At FY26 realization, 2,400 additional tonnes produce only ₹56.91 crore annual revenue at 100% utilization. Assuming a 19% EBITDA margin, annual depreciation of 5% of full project cost, 25.17% tax and 4% ONWC, a mature project earns 8.38% posttax on full committed capital; at 80% utilization it earns 6.02%. These are assumptions, not forecasts or proven project returns. They may understate returns if the shell supports later machinery/capacity, mix improves or depreciation economics differ, but no free additional capacity is credited. The model tests margins of 15%, 19% and 22% at utilization of 60%, 80%, 95% and 100%.

The historical FY23–FY26 incremental ROIC proxy is 21.62%, above the assumed 12–15% cost-of-capital range. It includes all CWIP and an explicit capital bridge, but benefits from higher use of legacy assets and cannot be projected automatically onto the new plant. CAP5 recognizes mixed investment generations rather than ignoring either strong history or weaker prospective full-cost economics. GQS 6.8 captures real, operating-led growth but does not establish an evidence-backed compounder. [S1][S5][S6]

sections.title: Management, Governance and Execution
sections.text:
The promoter family controls the company. Promoters alone hold approximately 63.84% post issue; promoter plus group holds about 70.98%. The fresh issue added 4,598,400 shares at ₹101 rather than cashing out through an OFS. The 26 July 2025 bonus shares are not economic dilution, but the IPO increases share count by 40.87% and dilutes a nonparticipating old holder by 29.02%. No warrants, convertibles or ESOP claims were disclosed in the final prospectus. Director remuneration was approximately ₹0.996 crore in FY26, about 8.72% of restated PAT. Related-party loans were interest-free at ₹3.1886 crore in June, with confirmations that repayment would not be required within 12 months. This support is positive but is not permanent equity.

Historical conduct needs balance. An Allahabad Bank loan became NPA and was assigned to OARPL. The company discloses an ₹18 crore FY2019 OTS, implemented settlement and withdrawal of the DRT matter. This is a historical default, not a current default. ROC's 16 July 2025 order imposed ₹2 lakh on the company and ₹0.5 lakh on each of four directors for the minimum-member deficiency. The prospectus says penalties were paid and a company secretary was appointed. Other delayed filings and incomplete promoter-relative information remain governance limitations. SEBI rejected the requested exemption and required public-domain disclosures. No substantiated diversion or repeated severe minority harm was established.

Observable delivery includes production of 3,215 tonnes in FY24, 4,154 in FY25 and 5,061.45 in FY26; installed capacity increased from 4,200 to 5,400 tonnes. The FY23 report described machinery/shed expansion, and subsequent production supports actual delivery. The next milestone is different: land is possessed, construction is underway and orders are placed, but January 2027 commissioning and customer qualification are unproved. Announced, financed, installed and revenue-generating assets must remain distinct. [S1][S4][S6][S8][S10]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Historical rows and formulas preserve scope, units and source differences. FY26 operating EBITDA of ₹22.8965 crore less D&A of ₹4.3879 crore gives EBIT of ₹18.5086 crore. Other income is ₹0.2813 crore; PAT of ₹11.4233 crore largely reflects operating earnings. A 25.17% normalized-tax proxy excludes other income rather than treating the prior tax-loss shield as perpetual. Current-share FY26 reported EPS is ₹7.21, versus pre-IPO restated EPS of ₹10.15. CFO is before financing interest, so the 1.926× FY24–FY26 cumulative CFO/PAT falls to 1.602× after a disclosed finance-cost proxy. FY26 CFO of ₹26.0288 crore minus asset cash capex of ₹25.6142 crore is ₹0.4146 crore. Subtracting ₹0.75 crore project advances and ₹3.1389 crore cash interest makes cash after those uses negative. Capex does not explain CFO; payables, receivables, inventory and advances do.

Receivables were ₹17.2032 crore, inventory ₹7.9355 crore and payables ₹23.6342 crore in March 2026. Average receivable days increased from 49.80 to 52.14 in FY26 despite almost flat year-end receivables, because the starting balance was high. End-balance days alone would misleadingly suggest a sharp improvement. All reported FY26 receivables were under six months and undisputed. Inventory WIP of ₹5.3855 crore, versus ₹1.7955 crore a year earlier, deserves attention. Payables increased by ₹6.9349 crore and supplier advances declined by ₹2.3065 crore, supporting CFO. Excluding these two releases leaves positive ₹16.7874 crore, but not all reported cash conversion is structural. FY23 also contains a ₹6.9117 crore advance release, so its exceptional conversion is not extrapolated.

The FY24 restatement adds ₹1.1266 crore interest to CFO and subtracts the same from financing cash. The auditor explicitly attributes it to a cell-link error; net cash is unchanged. FY24–FY26 PAT changes are small, disclosed salary/other-income and deferred-tax adjustments. The prospectus summary's FY26 investing labels are misaligned. The original audited cash flow correctly shows capital advance of −₹0.75 crore, interest received of +₹0.2667 crore and other noncurrent assets of −₹0.5918 crore, totaling approximately −₹26.6440 crore. The restated version splits a ₹2.163 crore FD reclassification without changing total investing cash. These resolved presentation differences are not evidence that cash disappeared.

Full statutory audit inspection found unmodified main and IFC opinions, positive edit-log reporting and no FY26 default. CARO says sanctioned working-capital limits did not exceed ₹5 crore, so no adverse bank-stock reconciliation is inferred. However, nil March capital commitments contrast with the final prospectus's dated PO schedule. Pre-March civil PO rows total about ₹4.8023 crore, with ₹4.7858 crore shown unpaid in September. These cannot be assumed to be March payables without execution/payment terms. A machinery quotation dated 15 December 2026 appears inconsistent with the September prospectus date. March new-land carrying value of ₹8.6565 crore, building CWIP of ₹18.4115 crore and advance of ₹0.75 crore also require reconciliation to September stated deployment of ₹25.2116 crore. Noncash financing, scope, timing or gross GST could explain differences, but no unsupported bridge is inserted. This material obligation/cash-perimeter issue keeps G2 on Hold, not a fraud verdict.

March cash equivalents were only ₹0.5683 crore. All ₹3.063 crore fixed deposits were pledged, including ₹2.163 crore classified current. June debt was ₹33.036 crore, including ₹4.95 crore of a ₹5 crore CC line backed by ₹1.25 crore deposits whose overlap with March deposits is unverified. GIDC land debt of ₹5.4081 crore was repaid by June. Net IPO proceeds of ₹41.3876 crore are approximately 96.54% earmarked for the remaining project of ₹39.9569 crore. Prepaid consultancy of ₹0.5201 crore is not automatically an additional IPO-cost refund. Tax of ₹3.2414 crore, CSR of ₹0.1282 crore and gratuity of ₹0.2247 crore are explicitly tracked. No hypothetical deposit release or uncommitted financing is treated as cash. [S1–S6][S8]

sections.title: Valuation and Market Expectations
sections.text:
The model links physical output × realization, operating margin, ONWC, maintenance and project capex, taxes, interest, debt repayment and operating cash. It does not extrapolate 30% growth indefinitely beyond 7,800 tonnes. FY27–FY32 annual units rise from 4,300 to 6,000 in bear, 5,500 to 7,600 in base and 5,600 to 7,800 in bull; annual realization grows by 0%, 2% and 3%. EBITDA margins span 12–14.5%, 18.5–19.5% and 20–22%, with terminal EBITDA multiples of 6×, 8× and 10×. Remaining project spending is ₹47.95 crore in bear, including a 20% overrun, and ₹39.9569 crore in base/bull. Maintenance capex is 3.5–4% of sales. Working capital is 16%, 6% and 3.5% of annual sales, versus the unusually lean FY26 ending ONWC. Required operating cash is the greater of ₹1.2 crore and 1% of annual sales.

The October starting balance is deliberately counterfactual: unrestricted cash of ₹2 crore, a project earmark of ₹39.9569 crore, debt of ₹30.636 crore and ONWC of ₹1.5496 crore. These are not reconstructed current balances. The pre-entry cash floor is unverified and never deemed passed. Old March tax and CSR are conservatively assumed still payable and tested where relevant; this is not a claim they were unpaid at cutoff. Deposits are never released. Intervals are half-open [April 1, next April 1); final FY32 cash uses 202/366 days to 20 October 2031. Terminal EBITDA interpolates FY31/FY32 consistently; post-terminal cash obligations do not govern this horizon.

All three central no-rescue paths breach their cash floor, with maximum notional gaps of ₹30.23 crore in bear, ₹6.34 crore in base and ₹2.30 crore in bull. Negative notional cash is a funding diagnostic, not available overdraft. All ordinary and conditional no-rescue IRRs and entry prices remain null, including stresses that appear funded after the hypothetical entry. Separate hypothetical equity rescues from the assumed October balances charge 3% fees and issue shares at 50% below the reference price. Gross equity is ₹31.16/6.53/2.37 crore, adding 6,708,693/1,406,388/510,018 shares. Holder dilution is 29.74/8.15/3.12%, distinct from share-count expansion of 42.33/8.87/3.22%. Counterfactual rescue IRRs are −8.90/18.54/30.25%. These do not repair unverified pre-entry gaps or establish available finance. Terminal equity subtracts debt, retained operating cash and the gratuity reserve; operational property is not added again.

At ₹92.90, reported post-IPO P/E is 12.89×. Proforma March equity plus estimated net IPO proceeds implies P/B of 1.82×, not an audited October book value. March-debt-only EV/EBITDA of 7.94× is explicitly stale; subtracting all IPO cash while omitting committed project spending would understate capital needs. No ordinary reverse-growth solution exists over a verified funded bracket. Sensitivities include units × exit multiple, 12/15/18% equity hurdles for counterfactual rescues, margin −3 percentage points, 12% ONWC, 20% project overrun, CC nonrenewal, one-year delay, higher maintenance, entry ONWC, opening cash and tax-already-paid alternatives, plus rescue discounts of 25/50/70% and fees of 0/3/6%. A perpetuity DCF is not forced on unproved plant returns. The explicit five-year cash/EV model is the intrinsic-return framework, with P/E and P/B as cross-checks. [S5][S6][M2]

sections.title: Bear Case and Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is that OEM program weakness or vendor resourcing hits a small set of customers just as the new unit adds fixed cost and cash obligations. Lower volumes reduce utilization and margin; more work-in-process and delayed customer receipts absorb cash; resin pass-through may lag; suppliers reduce credit; near-full CC utilization leaves little room to respond. A building and machinery package is not an instantly liquid reserve, and heavily discounted new equity transfers the cost of replacing cash to existing holders. The model combines these stresses rather than lowering EPS alone.

The bear counterfactual requires ₹31.16 crore gross new equity at a 50% discount and 3% fees, yet still produces approximately −8.90% annualized return, about 37.3% cumulative loss before personal taxes. Its ₹30.23 crore notional floor gap is a scenario output, not evidence of an actual missed payment. A complete loss of one large customer could be worse than the selected volume stress. The key thesis-break variable is sustainable cash after necessary reinvestment and debt service relative to verified unrestricted liquidity. Failure to qualify the new plant, irreversible program loss, uncollectible receivables or a proven commitment/funding deficit could permanently impair earning power; a temporary quoted drawdown alone does not.

Counterevidence is substantial: real production growth, positive operating cash, reduced largest-customer concentration, a completed IPO and no FY26 auditor-reported default. These prevent a claim of established insolvency or misconduct. Risk is High, not because SME status proves weakness, but because concentration, capital intensity and financing uncertainty can interact. [S4–S6][S8]

sections.title: 5× and 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold and tenfold share-price outcomes over five years require annual compounding of 37.97% and 58.49%. At unchanged current shares, 15× terminal P/E and a 10% net margin, 5× requires about ₹490.77 crore revenue and 10× requires ₹981.54 crore, compared with FY26 revenue of ₹120.01 crore. At FY26 realization, all 7,800 tonnes of announced capacity generate only ₹184.95 crore. Closing the gap requires much more capacity, mix/value addition, margins or valuation multiples. Each additional rupee of capital needs a funding and per-share bridge; a larger enterprise value alone is not a multibagger for an existing holder.

A lower terminal multiple, qualification delay, maintenance needs or rescue dilution raises the required operating scale. The current ₹65.17 crore project's full-cost return cross-check does not establish a repeatable high-return reinvestment engine. No precise probability is assigned. Classification: Speculative/unsupported at the five-year horizon, not mathematically impossible. [S5][S6][M2]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Reconcile nil March capital commitments with pre-March PO dates, work executed, cancellability, invoices and payment dates. The baseline is a ₹65.1685 crore budget and September deployment of ₹25.2116 crore. An auditor-supported bridge can clear G2; an actual undisclosed material obligation would escalate the concern.
2. Obtain recent published unrestricted cash, IPO utilization and remaining obligations. Baselines are March cash of ₹0.5683 crore, pledged FD of ₹3.063 crore and a project earmark of ₹39.9569 crore. An unfunded essential cash requirement is a thesis break; a missing update is a research hold, not default.
3. Track CC drawings against the ₹5 crore limit, June drawings of ₹4.95 crore, collateral FD of ₹1.25 crore and June 2027 renewal. Continued near-full utilization needs attention; actual withdrawal without replacement funding is material.
4. Check December 2026 approvals/customer trials and the January 2027 production target. A one-quarter delay requires reforecasting; inability to qualify commercial output while cash is depleted breaks the expansion thesis.
5. Track new-plant tonnes, realization, incremental EBIT and capital including land/CWIP. Require full-cost posttax returns above the 12–15% range rather than claiming the legacy 21.62% proxy for every new rupee.
6. Watch top-five customer dependence of 97.32%, largest-customer dependence of 30.99% and program awards. A major program loss needs linked volume, margin and cash stress; diversification requires recognized sales.
7. Monitor average DSO of 52.14 days, FY26 WIP of ₹5.3855 crore and payables of ₹23.6342 crore. Persistent growth in aged receivables or inventory alongside slower customer payments is a warning; realized credit losses are more decisive.
8. Test cash conversion after interest and payable/advance releases. The three-year baseline is 1.602× after the finance-cost proxy. Weak cash without an evidenced temporary bridge would reduce CASH.
9. Verify the ₹0.1282 crore CSR transfer and complete promoter-group/RPT disclosures, while preserving reported penalty payment and the closed OTS status.
10. Before implementation, recheck actual position, lot, restrictions, 20/60-session history, spreads and whole-lot order depth. The observed 17-session capacity estimate of 1.42 days is not an exit promise. This is a research review plan, not a trade instruction or a scheduled monitor. [S4–S6][S9][M1][M2]

sections.title: Final Classification and Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. The business has demonstrated genuine profitable growth, and latest multi-year cash conversion is better than a superficial growth-at-any-price story. But the new capital cycle has not yet earned its cost, and the obligation/cash bridge remains material to a new investment. GQS 6.8 is retained as arithmetic, not a ranking-eligible or compounder label. BQS and IAS remain NS because BAL and the investment factors cannot fairly be filled with neutral numbers. G2 also blocks favorable classification and quality ranking.

The research action is to wait for clarifying evidence, not buy because a conditional rescue case exceeds 15%. An existing holder would need their actual position and exit constraints assessed; no holdings, cost basis, personal tax details or allocation were supplied. Price can change upside, but cannot cure an unreconciled current funding position. A verified published cash/commitment bridge, sufficient stress resources and attributable new-plant results are the decisive evidence to revisit. Clean historical audits and strong sales already count positively. No proven severe governance failure or actual funding default is asserted. [S4–S6][M1][M2]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions and Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary financial evidence includes original FY23–FY26 statutory reports, full audit annexures, IPO restatements, the final prospectus, allotment announcement and official NSE listing, master and bhavcopy records. The ROC order is an official document obtained from a secondary mirror; its findings are cross-checked against the prospectus response. Machino's full annual report corrects a peer PAT/OCI label. Shaily is a qualitative capability comparator, not a transferable valuation multiple. Source URLs, dates, locators and SHA256 hashes accompany the evidence. Full financial tables and annual models are embedded in the canonical record.

Important unknowns are current unrestricted cash; capital commitment dates and cancellability; project book-versus-cash deployment; unspent net IPO proceeds and taxes/fees; whether prepaid consultancy relates to IPO costs already deducted; restricted FD overlap with June CC collateral; tax/CSR payments after March; qualification timing and attributable plant returns; current promoter-group completeness; and seasoned market depth. An unavailable filing is ND, not evidence of misconduct. Minor residual statement-drafting differences and explicitly bounded normalization assumptions are preserved.

Model assumptions are nominal INR, 25.17% tax, a 15% equity hurdle, a separate 12–15% capital-cost range, stated unit/realization/margin paths, maintenance capital and a cash floor. Rescue funding is counterfactual, not available finance. Raw issuer PDFs, HTML, OCR, page images, personal lists and identifiers are excluded from analytical backups. Safe financial extracts, model code/results, provenance and QA are retained. Offline reproduction checks arithmetic and artifact consistency, not fresh source authentication; original URLs and hashes permit a separate authentication step. This is non-personalized research, not investment advice or an execution recommendation. [S1–S11][P1][P2][M1][M2]
